steps.text: Place a piece of wax paper or foil on cookie sheet. Combine sugar, butter, milk and cocoa in medium saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to rolling boil.
Add peanut butter; stir to blend. Add oats, peanuts and vanilla; stir to mix well. Quickly drop mixture by heaping teaspoons onto wax paper or foil. Cool completely. Store in cool, dry place.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Cocoa No-Bake Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This recipe is one of the best no-bake cookie recipes I know. Enjoy!!

review.reviewBody: Awesome recipe best ones I have ever had. Only think I would add is the amount of time you should cook while at a boil. I used old fashon oats and it needed to boil for about 2-3 minutes for it to set properly. Must make again

Great recipe! I used old fashioned oats, and a touch of brown sugar. Other commenters are right, it needs to boil for a solid two minutes - but starting that countdown once you've got a full rolling boil is key. I omitted the peanuts and added an extra 1/3 - 1/2 cup of oats. Also, I bumped the vanilla to 1T. Super good, super easy to make - using a disher (little tiny ice cream scoop) makes them super easy to drop too!

We made this recipe last night and it was a huge hit -- tasted just like I remember from elementary school!

I did make a few modifications because we didn't have some of the ingredients. I used 3 squares of baker's unsweetened chocolate instead of cocoa, and 1 cup of extra chunky peanut butter since we didn't have peanuts. We also used brown sugar instead of white sugar, and I'll probably reduce it to 1 cup next time. It is very rich and flavorful.

Instead of individual cookies, we put the mixture into an 8 x 8 baking dish and cut it into bars when it cooled. They didn't turn out as firm as I would have liked, so I'll probably add more oats next time as others have suggested. I'm keeping this batch in the refrigerator and the coldness seems to keep them firm.

Thanks for sharing!

I use the same recipe called Fudgey Cocoa No-Bake Treats from Hershey's Best Loved Recipes book. I spoon the mixture into buttered metal cookie cutters placed on waxed paper and push them out after they harden or give as gifts still in the cookie cutters. I cut the recipe in half so that it doesn't set up in the pan while I'm filling the cookie cutters since this takes more time than spooning onto waxed paper.

I remember my Mom making these when we were growing up so I decided to make some for my son. They turned out great and whereas I usually make recipes following the instructions, I did make a couple of changes. I cut the sugar down to 1 cup because 2 cups seemed a bit excessive and they were definitely sweet enough. I also didn’t have quick cook oats on hand so I used old fashioned oats. I googled it and it said you could interchange the two in cooking but they suggested doing a couple of quick pulses in a food processor. I think that made all the difference with this recipe because it broke the oats down more so they wouldn’t be so hard to chew with this recipe. ***I did notice after making them that they didn’t seem to firm up very quickly like what I was used to. I tried putting them in the fridge for a while. We’ll see what happens.

This is a good recipe, and I modified it per other people's suggestions and my own preferences. I doubled it, used only 1.75 cups white sugar and .5 cups of Splenda brown. I put in a bit of extra peanut butter, and followed the suggestion of cooking the first 4 ingredients for a minute once they reached boiling and then adding peanut butter and cooking for another minute. Then I after I added the oats I also added half of a bag of dark chocolate chips (used special dark cocoa too.) What can I say, I'm a chocolate nut and I love the creamier texture you get by adding some real chocolate as well as cocoa. Turned out awesome!
Easy and always a success! I reduce the sugar by 1/2 cup and add the oats after the mixture boils.

This is a delicious and easy to make treat that with subtle tweaks can also be easy on the calories / sodium!

I cut the sugar to 1.5 cups, and used 1 cup brown & .5 white. I also used low fat, unsalted natural smooth peanut butter and crushed unsalted dry roasted peanuts. You'll never miss the salt when you savor them.

Each 2.5 to 3 inch blob: 147 calories and only 9 sodium!!!

I had to remake this about 3 times in order to get it right. do not cool for a minute!... add the hot mixture to oats asap... also make sure that the dough is not goopy.. if so add more oats. I tried this recipe with old fashioned oats firt, not a good idea. Use instant oats!

Great recipe! I substituted the butter with applesauce, sugar with stevia/maltodextrin mix, milk with lactose free nonfat milk, and peanut butter with Just Great Stuff chocolate peanut powder for a dairy free/ low sugar/ very low fat recipe. I spooned the mix onto the baking sheet with a tablespoon instead of a teaspoon and each large cookie comes out to roughly 30 calories.

Applesauce substituting is a little dicey with no-bakes, but the peanut powder absorbs the extra moisture quite well.

These cookies turned out exceptional. They were super easy to whip up with what ingredients I had in the house. I thought about using the steel cut oats I had to add some tougher texture, but was a little nervous to do so, and stuck with the instant oatmeal. I will definitely make these again and try the steel cut oats. I also added some coconut and some walnuts which added a little something special. These would be great to make with a child. Since they are shapeless, it would be fun for a child to help dollup the batter onto the sheets. I cooled them quickly in the fridge, and they were ready to eat right away.
I think I did something wrong because the mixture was very dry and didn't make fully formed cookies on the sheet. tastes insanely good though
I did 3/4 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup of brown sugar. Added a handful of semisweet chocolate chips and a pinch of salt.
These no bake are the best. They turned out just the way I expected them to and are a very good treat.
It was the best no bake cookies other than my grandma’s peanut butter no bake cookies.
it was super easy to make and because i didnt have an oven at the time it was perfect for us
I changed it by adding chocolate chips and didn't use peanuts and I also used a little less peanut butter and every buddy loved them. so good job!!!! also put some in Christmas tree formation.
My family loves these cookies! Try using almond butter instead of peanut butter. It kicks them up to 11.

This was the first thing my grandmother taught me how to make when I was little. She called them Cookie Candy. Still love them to this day. Easy to make and don't last very long because they are so good.
